purpose: Pinned inputs for the Windows x64 MSVC source build of the patched Codex CLI (native DeepSeek subagents) and its shareable zip bundle.

patch.normalization: UTF-8 without BOM, LF line endings, exactly one trailing newline

notes: dev-small inherits the upstream dev profile and sets opt-level 0, debug none, strip symbols. It keeps CI time and disk use far below a release build and matches the 'debug 0 / no incremental' requirement.
dev keeps debug="limited" unless the build script forces debug=0; it is heavier than dev-small.
release uses lto = "thin", codegen-units = 4 and is expected to be far slower on a 4-core GitHub-hosted runner. Use it only when a smaller, optimized binary is worth the extra minutes.
No profile in this repository has been executed on the MSVC CI runner yet; the workflow is new and its first run is the validation.

Filters are compiled Rust module paths, not file names. role.rs declares `#[path = "role_tests.rs"] mod tests;` inside module `agent::role`, so the test name prefix is `agent::role::tests`; the file name role_tests.rs would match nothing.
tools/handlers/multi_agents.rs declares `#[path = "multi_agents_tests.rs"] mod tests;`, so its test name prefix is `tools::handlers::multi_agents::tests`.
Each filter is wrapped in a nextest filterset `test(<name>)` predicate; the patterns are OR-ed into one -E expression.
--no-tests fail makes a run that matches zero tests exit non-zero instead of passing silently.
--test-threads 2 keeps Windows test subprocess contention down on a 4-core hosted runner.
The build script also resolves each unit filter against the checked-out source before running nextest, so a filter that no longer names a real module fails early.

buildReceipt.writtenBy: Step-Build, only after cargo build exits 0 and the binary is located
buildReceipt.requiredFor: Step-Package refuses to package without a receipt that matches the current plan and binary

runtimeManifest.consumer: scripts/DeepSeekNative.Common.ps1 -> Test-DseRuntimeManifest, discovered next to codex.exe using config/defaults.json -> runtimeManifestFileName

schema.version: string, plain workspace version (0.153.4); the installer compares this against its minimum version
schema.files: object map of file name -> lowercase sha256; the installer hashes each file in the same folder and requires no missing and no mismatched entries, which is why only the runtime executables are listed
schema.extraKeys: schemaVersion, product, kind, builtAtUtc, bundleName, buildProfile, toolchain and source{...} are ignored by the installer and carry provenance: source.commit is the patched openai/codex commit and source.patchSha256 is the digest of patches/codex-native-provider.patch
